podcast.title: Departure from Faith No More
podcast.body: Jim Martin was the guitarist for Faith No More during their successful period in the late 1980s and early 1990s. However, he was fired from the band in 1993 and has not returned since. "Jim Martin was the guitarist with Faith No More during their run in the late 80s and early 90s. But by 1993 things weren't going so great so he was fired and hasn't been back since."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Giant Pumpkin Grower
podcast.body: After his music career, Jim Martin developed a passion for competitively growing giant pumpkins at his home in Castro Valley, California, starting in 2000. In 2005, he grew a pumpkin weighing 1,087 pounds and was once named one of the five best giant pumpkin growers in America. "Instead, what he's done is developed a passion for, wait for it, growing giant pumpkins at his home in Castro Valley, California."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Reunion Announcement (2009)
xref.body: Despite previous denials of any reunion plans, the band announced their return on February 24, 2009, after a separation of 10 years, nine months, and 28 days. The reunion occurred without guitarist Jim Martin. "And on February 24th of 2009, 10 years, nine months, and 28 days after Billy Gould sent out that fax, they know more announced that they were, yes, getting back together."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Reunions: Some Lasted....and Sadly, Some Didn't ｜ Part 2

xref.title: Champion Pumpkin Grower
xref.body: Jim Martin is recognized as one of the most successful growers of champion pumpkins in the United States. "Jim Martin used to be a member of Faith No More is one of the greatest growers of champion pumpkins in all the United States."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Members' Post-Breakup Projects
xref.body: Following the breakup, members pursued various endeavors: other bands like Imperial Teen and Mr. Bungle were formed, some made guest appearances and received production credits, and record labels were established. Drummer Mike Bordin worked with Ozzy Osborne for a period, and guitarist Jim Martin transitioned to growing 1,300-pound pumpkins professionally. "Drummer Mike Bowden went off to work with Ozzy Osborne for a while."
